extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in mathematical physics / string theory studying BRST cohomology
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying the structural conditions, assumptions, and theorems needed to build and analyze quantum BRST complexes (Fock-space BRST quantization, cohomology, decomposition/Hodge theory, and semi-infinite Lie algebra cohomology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unimodularity condition (trace of adjoint zero)
rubrics_metrics.description: The condition ∑_{i,j} f_{ij}^j = 0 for all i (equivalently trad(b_i) = 0), i.e., that g be unimodular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the only condition needed for the inner product defined on the BRST complex to descend to cohomology in the presented polarization: if ∑_{i,j} f_{ij}^j = 0 then ∇1† = ±∇1 on integrable elements and coboundaries are orthogonal to cocycles (ker ∇1 ⊆ ker ∇1†). Physically this equals existence of a bi-invariant metric on the group manifold; failure means the inner product may not descend to cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and normalization of Berezin integral / inner product on forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix a non-zero top form ε ∈ Λ^k V* and define the Berezin integral by Ber ω = 0 for ω ∈ Λ^p≠k V* and Ber λ ε = λ. Define the inner product on forms by (ω, θ) = (−i)^p (k−p)! Ber(ω ∧ θ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These choices (including the factors of i) are motivated by hermiticity requirements of the prequantum inner product on KF(E). The normalization and choice of Hodge-type operator later are used to obtain a positive-definite inner product on the full Fock-space complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift ghost-number operator to make it skew-adjoint
rubrics_metrics.description: The ghost number operator N = ∑_{i=1}^k ε(c_i) ι(b_i) must be redefined by shifting it by an appropriate constant c so that N_c ≡ N − c is skew-adjoint; choosing c = k/2 achieves this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skew-adjointness of the ghost-number operator is used in grading properties and to ensure only inner products between opposite ghost numbers are non-zero; the shift is a concrete recipe provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrability / domain: integrable elements and finite-norm polarized sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare an element of KF(E) integrable if it belongs to Λ^k V* ⊗ Γ_F(E)_fin, where Γ_F(E)_fin denotes the polarized sections of finite norm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BRST and other operators are defined initially on integrable elements; one must check the constraints stabilize Γ_F(E)_fin so the BRST operator is densely defined. If M is compact (finite holomorphic sections) domain/closure issues disappear.

rubrics_metrics.name: BRST operator density/closedness and specification of domain
rubrics_metrics.description: The BRST operator ∇1 is generally unbounded; it must be specified on a dense domain (the integrable elements) and extended by closure to define the operator in the Hilbert space Γ_{F,L^2}(E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit specification of domain and closure matters because im ∇1 may be non-closed (infinite-dimensional) and factoring by a non-closed subspace causes topological issues (non-continuous surjection, non-complete quotient). Assumption that constraints stabilize integrable subspace is used to guarantee dense definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coboundaries orthogonal to cocycles (necessary for induced inner product)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require ker Q ⊆ ker Q† (i.e., BRST coboundaries are orthogonal to BRST cocycles) so that cohomology classes inherit a well-defined inner product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is equivalent to self-adjointness of Q in practical examples. The text emphasizes this is the necessary and sufficient condition for an inner product to descend to cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: BRST complex axioms: (F, Q, Ngh) structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A quantum BRST complex is a triple (F, Q, Ngh) where F is a Fock space graded by integer eigenvalues of a skew-self-adjoint ghost-number operator Ngh, and Q is a self-adjoint operator of degree +1 obeying Q^2 = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, assume a family {Λ} of self-adjoint mutually commuting operators commuting with Q and Ngh that decomposes F into finite-dimensional subspaces (or direct integrals). These finiteness and commuting assumptions are used repeatedly (e.g., to regularize traces and compute indices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefiniteness of the Fock-space inner product
rubrics_metrics.description: For a non-trivial BRST operator, the Fock space inner product must be indefinite (there must be null and negative-norm vectors); otherwise Q would be identically zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This observation explains why indefinite Fock spaces (ghosts/antighosts) are inherent to BRST quantization; it motivates later introduction of an involution C to obtain a positive-definite auxiliary inner product for Hodge-type arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of self-adjoint involution C to obtain positive-definite inner product
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce an involution C on each finite-dimensional eigenspace giving +1 on the positive-definite subspace and −1 on the negative-definite subspace; define a new positive-definite inner product ⟨ψ, φ⟩_C = ⟨ψ, C φ⟩.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C must map F_g → F_{−g} (so the new inner product pairs opposite ghost numbers). Using C one defines Q* = C Q C, and carries out the Hodge/decomposition arguments. Choice of C is not unique but results are independent up to pseudo-unitary transforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjointness and dual complex via Q*
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Q* = C Q C; then Q* is degree −1, obeys (Q*)^2 = 0, and provides the dual differential complex. The relation ker Q ⊆ ker Q* (after appropriate conditions) links the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dual complex is used to define harmonic subspace H = ker Q ∩ ker Q*, BRST Laplacian, and to prove decompositions and Poincaré-type duality H_g ≅ H_{−g}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition / Hodge theorem prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume positive-definite C-inner product and finite-dimensionality of the decomposition pieces so that F = im Q ⊕ ker Q* and ker Q = (ker Q ∩ ker Q*) ⊕ im Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under these hypotheses the projection onto harmonic subspace H induces an isomorphism H_g(F,Q) ≅ H ∩ F_g. The BRST Laplacian ' = Q Q* + Q* Q is self-adjoint with kernel = H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green's operator and invertibility on images
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the Green's operator G as a (partial) inverse to the BRST Laplacian on H⊥ = im Q ⊕ im Q*; G must commute with any operator commuting with the Laplacian and stabilize each finite subspace F_g(λ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invertibility of Q on im Q* (i.e., Q|_{im Q*} invertible with inverse G Q*) is used to solve homotopy relations and to show chain maps are chain-homotopic to their minimal extensions; requires ker Q ∩ im Q* = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism of operator BRST cohomology with End H(F)
rubrics_metrics.description: The operator cohomology H(ad_Q on End F) is isomorphic to End H(F): every cohomology class of endomorphisms is induced by a unique minimal extension from H, and chain homotopies can be constructed using the Green's operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surjectivity: extend maps on H to act trivially on im Q ⊕ im Q*. Injectivity: any chain map is chain-homotopic to its minimal extension; constructive homotopy uses Green's operator. This is used to relate operator cohomology and BRST harmonic vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing theorem and physical consistency (no-ghost)
rubrics_metrics.description: The vanishing theorem: H_g(F,Q) = 0 for g ≠ 0 (cohomology concentrated at ghost number 0). This vanishing is tied to consistency/unitarity: if it holds then operator cohomology is trivial except for endomorphisms of H0 and one can reduce the no-ghost theorem to index computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If vanishing fails, BRST quantization may produce physically inconsistent negative-norm states. The text emphasizes vanishing is both computationally convenient and physically desirable, though not proved in complete generality.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-ghost theorem reformulation: equality of Euler character and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the vanishing theorem, absence of negative-norm physical states is equivalent to ch_F = sgn_F (Euler characteristic equals signature), i.e., Tr_F( (−1)^{Ngh} ) = Tr_F C (and in graded form ch_q F = sgn_q F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One computes ch_F (Euler / character) and sgn_F (signature / trace of C) on finite eigenspaces; equality implies H0 has no negative-norm vectors. The index formulation: index_q D = ch_q F, allowing index-theoretic proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semi-infinite cohomology module and algebraic regularization conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: For semi-infinite cohomology of a graded Lie algebra g, require g to be graded of finite growth (dim g_m < ∞) and modules to satisfy finiteness hypotheses and to afford a projective representation whose cocycle cancels the Kac–Peterson class (or alternatively pass to an appropriate central extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conditions are necessary so that the semi-infinite differential squares to zero (d^2 = 0) after regularization. Two strategies: kill the Kac–Peterson cocycle by central extension, or tensor with a module affording the opposite projective class. These choices fix critical dimensions in string-theory examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical finiteness assumption for index computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume the family {Λ} of commuting self-adjoint operators has discrete spectrum and decomposes F into finite-dimensional eigenspaces F(λ) (dim F(λ) < ∞), so traces and graded traces (characters, signatures, indices) are defined as formal sums over λ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This finiteness is central to regularizing infinite-dimensional traces by computing on finite pieces and recombining as formal power series q^λ; used throughout for computing ch_q F, sgn_q F, and index_q D.
